No risk at Likelihood 3 or higher is unsettled. `bun tools/check-register.ts` exited 0. It checked 436 items and listed none in any of its four checks: not settled, settled with no `Verified` line, Moved Out for a live fault, or two Likelihood values.

The checker reads only the last `Status:` in each entry. So I ran a separate script over the register files and found 38 entries at Likelihood 3 or higher with more than one Status line. In all 38 the last Status is a settled one (closed, mitigated, or Moved Out), so none is currently unsettled. The earlier lines are the history: `open` or `partial` first, then `mitigated` or `closed`.

Two of those entries are settled only in part. The second is the only one where an earlier Status is not a plain `open` or `partial`:

- **RISK-067** (guards.md, Likelihood 4): the current Status is `mitigated 2026-11-19 for git`. The ask rules cover stash, hard reset, clean and `branch -D`, including the `git -C dir` form. For `rm`, Claude Code 2.1.327 refuses the dangerous forms on its own; the entry records fake-API probes for an empty variable, `./scratch/*` and `~/x/ *`. The entry says the disk-cleanup part "has no control; it rests on one report", with residual likelihood 2.
- **RISK-132** (handover.md, Likelihood 4): the current Status is `mitigated 2026-11-19 for options the user refused`, because the handover keeps every user correction, refusal and consent word for word (`hooks/handover/text.ts:14`). It is "accepted" for an option the agent ruled out alone, where the next session rechecks it against the code. The entry's `Verified` line says the 2026-11-19 dogfood handover was not re-read.
- **RISK-416** (edit.md, Likelihood 5): its Status history is `closed`, then `reopened`, then `mitigated`. It was reopened because a dogfood run used `sed -i` and failed on BSD flags. The current `mitigated 2026-11-19` rests on one output-style line telling the model to use `perl -pi`, with 3 of 3 runs on perl. That depends on the model following the line, not on a hard control.

I read the entries and the checker source. I did not re-run the probes or tests the entries cite.
